q: Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in _____.
e: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature. Mass or volume is not this quantity.

q: The unit of heat is _____ in SI unit.
e: Heat is energy, so the SI unit is the joule. The unit of heat is joule (J) in SI unit. Calorie (cal) or watt (w) is not this quantity.

q: The heat unit in the CGS system is _____.
e: CGS still uses the calorie for heat. The heat unit in the CGS system is calorie (cal). Do not trade calorie (cal) for kilocalorie (kcal) or British thermal unit (Btu).

q: The heat unit in the MKS system is _____.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. The heat unit in the MKS system is kilocalorie (kcal). Joule (j) or calorie (cal) is not this quantity.

q: The heat unit in the British system is the _____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The heat unit in the British system is the British thermal unit (Btu). Do not trade British thermal unit (Btu) for foot-pound (ft-lb) or kilocalorie (kcal).

q: Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 _____.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie. Do not trade kilocalorie for calorie or joule.

q: The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is _____ J.
e: Mayer's mechanical equivalent of heat is 1 cal = 4.184 J. The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J. 1.356 or 1055 is not this quantity. 4.184 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 kcal = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 kcal = 4184 J. 1055 or 1.356 is not this quantity. 4184 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 Btu = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 Btu = 1055 J. Do not trade 1055 for 4184 or 1.356. 1055 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 ft-lb = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. Do not trade 1.356 for 4.184 or 1055. 1.356 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and _____ energy of the molecules.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and temperature energy of the molecules. Do not trade temperature for pressure or potential.

q: The kinetic energy of molecules is directly related to _____.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The kinetic energy of molecules is directly related to temperature. Chemical or nuclear is not this quantity.

q: The potential energy is energy due to _____ between the molecules.
e: Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing. The potential energy is energy due to inter-molecular forces between the molecules. Do not trade inter-molecular forces for gravitational forces or magnetic forces.

q: The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the _____ between the molecules.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the distance between the molecules. Do not trade distance for mass or charge.

q: The internal energy of the substance is known as its _____.
e: Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing. The internal energy of the substance is known as its thermal energy. Do not trade thermal energy for mechanical energy or electrical energy.

q: The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as _____.
e: The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as heat. Work or power is not this quantity.

q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the _____ of the object.
e: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity of the object. Do not trade thermal capacity for specific heat capacity or latent heat.

q: The formula for thermal capacity of an object is $C =$ _____.
e: The formula for thermal capacity of an object is C = (ΔQ)/(ΔT). (ΔT)/(ΔQ) or m c ΔT is a different relation from (ΔQ)/(ΔT).

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is _____ per kelvin (J K$^{-1}$).
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1). Calorie or watt is not this quantity.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a _____ of the material it is made of.
e: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of. Color or shape is not this quantity.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is called _____.
e: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is called molar thermal capacity. Specific heat capacity or latent heat capacity is not this quantity.

q: The formula for molar thermal capacity is $C =$ _____.
e: The formula for molar thermal capacity is C = (ΔQ)/(n ΔT). (ΔQ)/(m ΔT) or (ΔT)/(n ΔQ) is a different relation from (ΔQ)/(n ΔT).

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin. Celsius or fahrenheit is not this quantity.

q: The thermal capacity per unit mass of a substance is the _____.
e: The thermal capacity per unit mass of a substance is the specific heat capacity. Molar thermal capacity or latent heat is not this quantity.

q: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat needed to change the temperature of a _____ of that substance by one degree.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat needed to change the temperature of a unit mass of that substance by one degree. Unit volume or unit mole is not this quantity.

q: The formula for specific heat capacity is $c =$ _____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The formula for specific heat capacity is c = (C)/(m). (m)/(C) or C m is a different relation from (C)/(m).

q: By rewriting the specific heat capacity equation, the amount of heat is $\Delta Q =$ _____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. By rewriting the specific heat capacity equation, the amount of heat is ΔQ = m c ΔT. (m c)/(ΔT) or (m ΔT)/(c) is a different relation from m c ΔT.

q: In the SI units, the unit of the specific heat capacity is joule per _____ per kelvin (J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$).
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. In the SI units, the unit of the specific heat capacity is joule per kilogram per kelvin (J kg^-1 K^-1). Do not trade kilogram for gram or mole.

q: Other units used for the specific heat capacity are kcal kg$^{-1}$ $^{\circ}$C$^{-1}$ and _____ g$^{-1}$ $^{\circ}$C$^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. Other units used for the specific heat capacity are kcal kg^-1 °C⁻¹ and cal g^-1 °C⁻¹. Joule or kilocalorie is not this quantity.

q: According to Table 5.1, the specific heat capacity of water is _____ J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. According to Table 5.1, the specific heat capacity of water is 4184 J kg^-1 K^-1. Do not trade 4184 for 2089 or 1963.

q: According to Table 5.1, the specific heat capacity of ice (-10 $^{\circ}$C to 0 $^{\circ}$C) is _____ J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. According to Table 5.1, the specific heat capacity of ice (-10 °C to 0 °C) is 2089 J kg^-1 K^-1. 4184 or 385 is not this quantity.

q: According to Table 5.1, the substance with the highest specific heat capacity is _____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. According to Table 5.1, the substance with the highest specific heat capacity is Hydrogen (gas). Water or helium (gas) is not this quantity.

q: When heat is transferred from one object to another object, the total heat lost by one object is equal to the total _____ by the other object.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. When heat is transferred from one object to another object, the total heat lost by one object is equal to the total heat gained by the other object. Do not trade heat gained for work done or energy lost.

q: Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of _____ of energy.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of conservation of energy. Do not trade conservation for transformation or dissipation.

q: A calorimeter is a device used to measure the _____ of a chemical reaction or physical change.
e: A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water. A calorimeter is a device used to measure the heat flow of a chemical reaction or physical change. Do not trade heat flow for temperature change or pressure change.

q: A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of copper or _____.
e: A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water. A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of copper or aluminium. Iron or lead is not this quantity.

q: The metallic vessel with a stirrer is kept in an insulating jacket to prevent heat lost to the _____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The metallic vessel with a stirrer is kept in an insulating jacket to prevent heat lost to the environment. Do not trade environment for surrounding water or thermometer.

q: Most substances can exist in three states, i.e., solid, liquid and _____.
e: Most substances can exist in three states, i.e., solid, liquid and gas. Plasma or vapour is not this quantity.

q: A transition from one of the three states to another is called a _____.
e: A transition from one of the three states to another is called a phase change. Thermal expansion or heat exchange is not this quantity.

q: The change from one phase to another takes place very abruptly at a definite _____.
e: The change from one phase to another takes place very abruptly at a definite temperature. Pressure or volume is not this quantity.

q: The temperature at which a phase change occurs depends on _____.
e: The temperature at which a phase change occurs depends on pressure. Mass or volume is not this quantity.

q: The energy absorbed or liberated by a substance in a phase change is called the _____.
e: The energy absorbed or liberated by a substance in a phase change is called the latent heat. Sensible heat or thermal capacity is not this quantity.

q: The energy absorbed or liberated by a unit mass of substance in a phase change is called the _____.
e: The energy absorbed or liberated by a unit mass of substance in a phase change is called the specific latent heat. Molar latent heat or thermal capacity is not this quantity.

q: If $L$ is the specific latent heat of an object, the heat needed to change the phase of that object of mass $m$ is $\Delta Q =$ _____.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. If L is the specific latent heat of an object, the heat needed to change the phase of that object of mass m is ΔQ = L m. (L)/(m) or (m)/(L) is a different relation from L m.

q: The SI unit of specific latent heat is _____ per kilogram (J kg$^{-1}$).
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The SI unit of specific latent heat is joule per kilogram (J kg^-1). Do not trade joule for calorie or watt.

q: The change from the solid phase directly to the gas phase is called _____.
e: The change from the solid phase directly to the gas phase is called sublimation. Do not trade sublimation for vaporization or condensation.

q: Sublimation is used in the _____ process which does not damage food and preserves its quality and taste.
e: Sublimation is used in the freeze-drying process which does not damage food and preserves its quality and taste. Pasteurization or fermentation is not this quantity.

q: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called _____.
e: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called vaporization. Do not trade vaporization for condensation or fusion.

q: The temperature at which a liquid vaporizes under normal pressure is called its _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The temperature at which a liquid vaporizes under normal pressure is called its boiling point. Melting point or critical point is not this quantity.

q: Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of _____.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of vaporization. Fusion or condensation is not this quantity.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is _____ J kg$^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2.255 × 10^6 J kg^-1. 3.335 × 10^5 or 4.184 × 10³ is a different relation from 2.255 × 10^6.

q: The change of vapour or gas phase into liquid phase is called _____.
e: The change of vapour or gas phase into liquid phase is called condensation. Vaporization or sublimation is not this quantity.

q: In condensation, the substance _____ heat.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In condensation, the substance releases heat. Do not trade releases for absorbs or transforms.

q: In vaporization, the substance _____ heat.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In vaporization, the substance absorbs heat. Releases or reflects is not this quantity.

q: The temperature at which a solid melts under normal pressure is called the _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The temperature at which a solid melts under normal pressure is called the melting point. Boiling point or triple point is not this quantity.

q: The melting point for ice under normal pressure is _____ $^{\circ}$C.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The melting point for ice under normal pressure is 0 °C. -10 or 100 is not this quantity.

q: Heat required to melt 1 kg of a solid at its melting point is called the specific latent heat of _____.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. Heat required to melt 1 kg of a solid at its melting point is called the specific latent heat of fusion. Do not trade fusion for vaporization or condensation.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is _____ J kg$^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The exact value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.335 × 10^5 J kg^-1. 2.255 × 10^6 or 4.184 × 10³ is a different relation from 3.335 × 10^5.

q: According to Table 5.2, the melting point of ethyl alcohol is _____ $^{\circ}$C.
e: According to Table 5.2, the melting point of ethyl alcohol is -114 °C. Do not trade -114 for 0 or -39. -114 is what this sentence is naming.

q: According to Table 5.2, the boiling point of mercury is _____ $^{\circ}$C.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. According to Table 5.2, the boiling point of mercury is 357 °C. 100 or 960 is not this quantity.

q: The melting point and boiling point vary with _____.
e: The melting point and boiling point vary with pressure. Do not trade pressure for mass or volume.

q: At the _____ point, liquid, solid and vapour phase may all exist together.
e: At the triple point, liquid, solid and vapour phase may all exist together. Critical or boiling is not this quantity.

q: At the critical point, both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same _____, and are therefore indistinguishable.
e: At the critical point, both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same density, and are therefore indistinguishable. Temperature or pressure is not this quantity.

q: The melting point of ice _____ as the pressure increases.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The melting point of ice decreases as the pressure increases. Increases or remains constant is not this quantity.

q: For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates lower the melting point of ice and _____ the ice under them.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates lower the melting point of ice and melts the ice under them. Do not trade melts for freezes or sublimes.

q: An increase in external pressure will _____ the boiling point of water.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. An increase in external pressure will raise the boiling point of water. Do not trade raise for lower or maintain.

q: When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is _____ the normal atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is twice the normal atmospheric pressure. Equal to or half is not this quantity.

q: In a pressure cooker, water boils at a higher temperature of _____ $^{\circ}$C.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. In a pressure cooker, water boils at a higher temperature of 120 °C. 100 or 150 is not this quantity.
